verified_against_binary: v2.36.5 is a discoverability pass on the published site. No fact changes. Audit found the content-side foundations already strong -- unique question-shaped H1s that match how authors actually search, unique titles and meta descriptions, lang, viewport, inline CSS, clean URLs -- and four mechanical gaps: no sitemap.xml, no robots.txt, no canonical, no social or structured-data tags. All four are now generated. Sitemap and robots are emitted from the same doc.pages loop that emits the pages, so a new page cannot exist without appearing in the sitemap; a test asserts the count. Canonical points at the apex, which is correct because both www and the github.io origin already 301 there (checked, not assumed). Structured data is TechArticle + BreadcrumbList, deliberately NOT FAQPage: Google has restricted FAQ rich results to a narrow set of authoritative sites since 2023, so FAQ markup would claim a result these pages will not get. The .md twins stay crawlable on purpose -- they are the LLM-facing copy and every HTML page now declares itself canonical, so they cannot split ranking. 404 is noindex; /static/ is disallowed. Also fixed a real bug in the build's own link gate, which resolved root-absolute hrefs against each page's directory and reported /favicon.svg as missing from every page.
note: Not done, and deliberately: no OG image (a summary card without one is honest for a text reference; a generated image is a maintenance burden that adds nothing to ranking), and no analytics.
